title: Short Stuff: Haunted Real Estate
summary: Short Stuff episode on haunted real estate and whether sellers must disclose that a home is haunted. The hosts open with banter about a personal haunted-house question and a recommended horror series, then discuss the 1990s New York case Stambovski v. Achtley, in which a buyer sued over an undisclosed haunting and an appeals court reversed the lower court's buyer-beware ruling. They cover the legal logic (material defect, disclosure), Minnesota's disclosure law on paranormal activity, real estate broker Cindy Hagley's views on disclosure, and stigmatized properties such as homicides and suicides, noting that Alaska, California and South Dakota require disclosure of deaths. The episode closes with a teaser for the Halloween episode and a sign-off.

segments.title: Opening banter and haunted house question
segments.summary: The hosts joke about the episode's subject and whether a home they know could be haunted, then trade recommendations for the horror series The Haunting of Bly Manor and tease the scary season.

segments.title: Stambovski v. Achtley lawsuit
segments.summary: The hosts explain that a seller who does not disclose a haunting can be sued. They describe Helen Achtley, who publicized her upstate New York Victorian as haunted, and buyer Jeffrey Stambovski, who sued after learning of it. The trial judge ruled buyer beware, but an appeals court reversed that and held the house haunted as a matter of law.

segments.title: Legal reasoning and disclosure rules
segments.summary: The hosts discuss caveat emptor versus material defect, noting that no state requires disclosure of haunting. They mention Minnesota's law, which exempts sellers from disclosing non-material facts including perceived paranormal activity, and say the New York ruling may serve as precedent elsewhere.

segments.title: Cindy Hagley on disclosing haunted homes
segments.summary: California real estate broker Cindy Hagley, who runs Past Life Homes, advises disclosing haunting when it affects value or when it is open and notorious, and says a direct question should be answered honestly.

segments.title: Stigmatized properties and deaths in homes
segments.summary: The hosts define stigmatized or psychologically affected property, including homes with murders, meth labs, or reported hauntings. They note that most states do not require disclosure of deaths, but Alaska, California and South Dakota do require disclosure ahead of sale.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts wrap up the haunted real estate topic and sign off with the show's credits.
